english.title: Conspire to intentionally / recklessly cause a public nuisance
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, conspired together with **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to

(A)_[do an act,]_
(B)_[omit to do an act that you were required to do by enactment or rule of law,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ACT OR OMISSION..), and that

(C)_[created a risk or caused serious harm to the public or a section of the public]_
(D)_[obstructed the public or a section of the public in the exercise or enjoyment of a right that may be exercised or enjoyed by the public at large]_

intending or being reckless that it would have such a consequence
english.legislation: Contrary to section 78(1) and (4) of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from the 28th June 2022 due to changes made by the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 which abolished the common law offence of public nuisance and replaced it with a statutory offence. For the offence applying before the 28th June 2022, see H9423.
(ii) It is a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove they had a reasonable excuse for any act or omission - 78(3).
(iii) Case-by-case review of MoPI group required for offence due to range of situations covered.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:None
